text:
OpenQodex

 
 
 
 

Open source AI code review for coding agents. A separate reviewer checks every change your agent writes before you push. A code graph gives your agent a map of your codebase. Works in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Cline and Goose.

For people, in your terminal:

 

After the install, say to your agent: "review my change with openqodex".

 

The report page of an OpenQodex review at its findings, captured 2026-10-25 with openqodex 0.14.0 and reviewer claude 2.1.310, on the openqodex/openqodex-lp repository.

The landing page: 

AI agents: read the agent guide. After the install, /.openqodex/bin/openqodex guide for-agents prints the guide for the installed version.

OpenQodex reviews your code change before you push it. Your change is the commits you have not pushed plus everything uncommitted. OpenQodex runs on your machine, from your coding agent or your terminal.

First, OpenQodex runs the scanners that fit the files you changed. A scanner is a program that checks code without a model, such as gitleaks or semgrep. A finding is one problem at one place in the code, with a severity. OpenQodex keeps the scanner findings on the lines you changed. It drops findings in test fixtures and in rules you switched off. Every supported lockfile in the repository is checked against osv.dev at every review and scan of a change. It skips the paths you exclude. Advisories outside the changed lines are shown, never counted, and kept out of the reviewer's brief. Each advisory names its fixed versions, or says no fixed version is published.

Then OpenQodex starts reviewers: separate Claude Code or Codex processes on your own login. By default, a reviewer is a fresh process of the agent you work in, with no memory of your session. When that agent cannot review, or you run review in a terminal, OpenQodex starts the first agent that can. Finder sessions read each part of the change, with the code that calls it, and propose candidates with a quoted line as evidence. A script checks every quote against the code. Verifier sessions then judge each candidate and each scanner finding against the code, and must confirm or refute every one with a reason. Scripts check that every scanner finding was answered and that every changed line was given to a reviewer. Style and naming notes are shown as observations and do not block. Then you choose which findings your agent fixes.

 Where it runs

 Coding agent Starts a review Can be the reviewer Push gate 
 --- --- --- --- 
 Claude Code yes yes yes 
 Codex CLI yes yes yes, after you trust the hook in Codex 
 Cursor yes no no, a rule asks Cursor to review 
 Cline yes no no, a rule asks Cline to review 
 Goose yes no no, the hints ask Goose to review 

In Cursor, Cline and Goose, the review needs Claude Code or Codex installed as the reviewer. A push gate is a hook that looks for a review before your agent runs git push .

 Requirements

- Node 22 or newer, and git.
- macOS or Linux. CI runs the gate on Node 22, on macOS and on Ubuntu Linux. No test runs on Windows or WSL.
- For a full review: Claude Code or Codex, installed and logged in. OpenQodex needs no account or API key of its own.
- Some scanners need a language runtime that OpenQodex does not install. brakeman and rubocop need Ruby. golangci-lint needs Go. cargo-deny needs Cargo.

 Install

In a terminal, init finds Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, Cline and Goose on your machine. It lists the files it will write. It asks you once. It starts the scanner downloads that your repository needs. Then it reviews your current change when a reviewer can start.

In your own terminal, run /.openqodex/bin/openqodex review . That path is the launcher, a small script that init writes. An npx install puts no openqodex on your PATH .

For agents, the same install with no question:

To install only the skill, run npx skills add openqodex/openqodex -g . That installs no push gate and downloads no scanner. A later init replaces that skill with the skill that init installs.

OpenQodex itself collects no usage data. The built-in scanners, as OpenQodex runs them, send no code. The reviewer sends your change to the model service of your Claude Code or Codex login. The privacy page lists each network use of this version.

 

 What it does today

- openqodex review reviews your change in one command.
- It writes report.html , report.md , report.json and report.sarif . SARIF is a standard JSON format for scanner results.
- At the end, it prints a receipt. The receipt holds the verdict, one line per finding and the path of report.html . Here is an example report.
- The skill tells your agent to show you the receipt. It tells the agent to ask "Fix all, or tell me which?". It tells the agent to fix only the findings you name.
- review --all reviews every file of the repository, less the paths that review.paths.exclude leaves out.
- review reviews a branch. review ' 42' reviews a pull request.
- A review is complete only when every stage ran. Otherwise, review prints "Review incomplete" with what is missing. Then it exits 2.
- The push gate inside your agent looks for a review of your current work. It does not know what a push sends. For a plain git push (also after one leading cd && , with the folder as a full path or one starting with ./ or ../ , judged in that folder, and with its output trimmed, as in 2 &1 tail -5 ), it asks whether your current work has a passing review. For any other push command, it says it cannot tell. The git pre-push hook that init adds checks the exact commits a push sends, for each git push that runs git hooks. git push --no-verify skips that hook. A review of the change being pushed that did not finish never blocks that push; the hook says so in one line.
